description.value: The study quantified abnormal eating behavior and sucrose preference in behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia and semantic dementia and identified their neural correlates using voxel-based morphometry of high-resolution structural MRI.

spans.text: The present study aimed to (1) quantify eating behavior in patients with bvFTD and semantic dementia using ecologically valid methods, notably an ad libitum breakfast and sucrose preference approach, and (2) identify the neural correlates of these eating behaviors using voxel-based morphometry analyses of high-resolution structural brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

description.value: Observational study comparing four participant groups, with eating behavior assessed by an ad libitum breakfast meal, dessert preference testing, questionnaires, and structural MRI.

spans.text: The present study aimed to (1) quantify eating behavior in patients with bvFTD and semantic dementia using ecologically valid methods, notably an ad libitum breakfast and sucrose preference approach, and (2) identify the neural correlates of these eating behaviors using voxel-based morphometry analyses of high-resolution structural brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
This study applied novel, ecologically valid methods to quantify food intake and sucrose preference in bvFTD and semantic dementia, which share clinical and pathologic features.

name.value: Ad libitum breakfast test meal and dessert experiment

description.value: Participants consumed an ad libitum buffet-style breakfast after fasting, and later rated and consumed desserts varying in sucrose content to measure total caloric intake, food preferences, and sucrose preference.

instructions.value: Participants were asked to eat until comfortably full and to rate how much they liked each dessert and how sweet it was.

stimuli.value: Buffet-style breakfast foods and Eton mess desserts containing 26%, 39%, and 60% sucrose.
